Pooled held-out scores of the random forest feature ablation (run `ablation`), every
input configuration with its 5x5 window statistics and on the run's common support.
The columns are grouped by the pixels they are computed over: IoU, AUC and precision
over all scope pixels, recall over glacier pixels only, and the edge false-positive
rate over the non-glacier pixels within 30 m outside the outlines. Every row also
gives its number of input layers. The rows are grouped by input: GLACE and the subsets
of its layers, the single-pass composites, and the global seasonal product. Two
variants: with the edge false-positive rate, and with the recall split into clean and
debris-covered ice instead. Each is printed as a booktabs `tabular` in the layout of
`tab:rf` in the paper and saved in `FIGURE_DIR`. A figure follows the IoU per glacier
across the debris-covered fraction of its area.

## Metrics

Every scope pixel is classified at the threshold of the fold that held its tile out,
and the confusion counts are pooled over the folds: TP and FN are glacier pixels
predicted as glacier and as non-glacier, FP and TN non-glacier pixels predicted as
glacier and as non-glacier.

| Metric | Pixels | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AUC | all | Area under the ROC curve of the predicted glacier probability |
| IoU | all | TP / (TP + FP + FN) |
| Precision | all | TP / (TP + FP) |
| Recall | glacier | TP / (TP + FN); clean and debris-covered ice split by the SGI debris flag |
| Edge FPR | non-glacier, 0 < d ≤ 30 m | FP / (FP + TN) |

The edge false-positive rate is the share of non-glacier pixels in the edge band that
are classified as glacier. The band holds every non-glacier pixel whose signed distance
$d$ to the outlines of its acquisition year lies in $0 < d \le 30$ m: $d$ is negative
inside a glacier and positive outside, from a Euclidean distance transform of the
rasterized outlines with a 1 km halo, so a tile border does not create an edge. The
band has no glacier pixels, so it measures only how far a model's glacier extent
spills over the outline:

$$
\mathrm{FPR}_\mathrm{edge} = \frac{\mathrm{FP}_\mathrm{edge}}{\mathrm{FP}_\mathrm{edge} + \mathrm{TN}_\mathrm{edge}}
$$

```{python}
from matplotlib.colors import to_rgba
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib_inline.backend_inline import set_matplotlib_formats
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from glace_production.config import settings
from glace_production.plotting import add_grid, set_context, set_style
from glace_production.validation.config import DatasetConfig, RunConfig
from glace_production.validation.store import ValidationStore

set_style()
set_context("paper")
set_matplotlib_formats("retina")
```

## Configuration

```{python}
TABLE_NAME = "rf-ablation"  # saved as {TABLE_NAME}-{variant}.tex in FIGURE_DIR
FIGURE_DIR = settings.figures_dir / TABLE_NAME  # one folder per notebook
FIGURE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
RUN = "ablation"
MODEL = "rf"

# Row groups of the table, in order: (heading, {feature set: row label}). The rows of a
# group with a heading are set under it, indented; a group without one stands alone.
# Unless the label says otherwise, an input is coherence and backscatter in VV and VH
# (the global seasonal product has no VH coherence); the caption says so.
GROUPS = [
    (
        "GLACE",
        {
            "all_ctx": "All layers",
            "vv_ctx": "VV only",
            "vh_ctx": "VH only",
            "coh_dual_ctx": "Coherence only",
            "rtc_dual_ctx": "Backscatter only",
        },
    ),
    (
        "Single-pass composites",
        {
            "pass_ctx": "Both as separate inputs",
            "asc_ctx": "Ascending only",
            "desc_ctx": "Descending only",
        },
    ),
    ("", {"gs_ctx": "Global seasonal"}),
]
SETS = {fs: label for _, rows in GROUPS for fs, label in rows.items()}

# (group_by, group, metric) -> column label; group None is the pooled score
COLUMNS = {
    "iou": (("all", None, "iou"), "IoU"),
    "auc": (("all", None, "auc"), "AUC"),
    "precision": (("all", None, "precision"), "Precision"),
    "recall": (("all", None, "recall"), "Recall"),
    "clean": (("debris", "clean", "recall"), "Clean"),
    "debris": (("debris", "debris", "recall"), "Debris"),
    "edge_fpr": (("band", "edge", "fpr"), "Edge FPR"),
}
LAYERS = "Layers"  # column of the number of input layers, before the scores

# Variant -> column groups (header, columns); an empty header gets no rule
VARIANTS = {
    "edge": [
        ("", ["layers"]),
        ("All pixels", ["iou", "auc", "precision"]),
        ("Glacier", ["recall"]),
        ("Non-glacier", ["edge_fpr"]),
    ],
    "debris": [
        ("", ["layers"]),
        ("All pixels", ["iou", "auc", "precision"]),
        ("Glacier pixels", ["recall", "clean", "debris"]),
    ],
}
```

## Data

```{python}
store = ValidationStore.default()
metrics = store.read_parquet(store.metrics_path(RUN))
metrics = metrics[(metrics.model == MODEL) & metrics.feature_set.isin(SETS)]


def column(group_by: str, group: str | None, metric: str) -> pd.Series:
    """One score per feature set."""
    rows = metrics[(metrics.group_by == group_by) & (metrics.metric == metric)]
    if group is not None:
        rows = rows[rows.group == group]
    return rows.set_index("feature_set")["value"]


scores = pd.DataFrame({key: column(*spec) for key, (spec, _) in COLUMNS.items()}).reindex(
    list(SETS)
)
```

The number of input layers of a feature set is read from the configs the run and its
datasets were stamped with: the columns that are measurement layers, without their
window statistics (each layer enters as its value, 5x5 mean and 5x5 standard
deviation).

```{python}
run = RunConfig.from_yaml(store.run_dir(RUN) / "config.yaml")
layer_names = {
    name
    for dataset in run.datasets
    for name in DatasetConfig.from_yaml(
        store.samples_dir(dataset) / "config.yaml"
    ).measurement_layers
}
scores["layers"] = pd.Series(
    {fs: sum(c in layer_names for c in run.feature_sets[fs]) for fs in SETS}
).reindex(list(SETS))
scores.rename(index=SETS).round(3)
```

## LaTeX

No value is set in bold: the rows differ in their number of input layers, so the
best value of a column does not rank comparable inputs. The table is written line by
line, indented as in the paper's `main.tex`, so that it replaces the `tabular` there
unchanged: a `\multicolumn` header over each titled column group with a `\cmidrule`
below it, a heading row above each titled row group, its rows indented by `\quad`, and
an `\addlinespace` between the row groups.

```{python}
INDENT = "    "  # of every line, as in main.tex


def booktabs(groups: list[tuple[str, list[str]]]) -> str:
    """Booktabs tabular of the given column groups, with the rows grouped as in GROUPS."""
    keys = [k for _, cols in groups for k in cols]
    n_cols = 1 + len(keys)
    titles, rules, first = [""], [], 2
    for title, cols in groups:
        if title:
            titles.append(
                rf"\multicolumn{{{len(cols)}}}{{c}}{{{title}}}" if len(cols) > 1 else title
            )
            rules.append(rf"\cmidrule(lr){{{first}-{first + len(cols) - 1}}}")
        else:
            titles += [""] * len(cols)
        first += len(cols)
    names = ["Input"] + [LAYERS if k == "layers" else COLUMNS[k][1] for k in keys]

    def cell(fs: str, k: str) -> str:
        value = scores.loc[fs, k]
        if pd.isna(value):
            return "--"
        return f"{value:.0f}" if k == "layers" else f"{value:.3f}"

    lines = [
        rf"\begin{{tabular}}{{l{'c' * len(keys)}}}",
        r"\toprule",
        " & ".join(titles) + r" \\",
        "".join(rules),
        " & ".join(names) + r" \\",
        r"\midrule",
    ]
    for i, (heading, rows) in enumerate(GROUPS):
        if i:
            lines.append(r"\addlinespace")
        if heading:
            lines.append(rf"\multicolumn{{{n_cols}}}{{l}}{{{heading}}} \\")
        for fs, label in rows.items():
            row = (r"\quad " if heading else "") + label
            lines.append(" & ".join([row] + [cell(fs, k) for k in keys]) + r" \\")
    lines += [r"\bottomrule", r"\end{tabular}"]
    return "\n".join(INDENT + line for line in lines)


for variant, groups in VARIANTS.items():
    latex = booktabs(groups)
    (FIGURE_DIR / f"{TABLE_NAME}-{variant}.tex").write_text(latex + "\n")
    print(f"% variant: {variant}\n{latex}\n")
```

## Accuracy versus debris cover

The glaciers are binned by the debris-covered fraction of their area (SGI2023 debris
flag). Every statistic weights a glacier by its glacier pixels, so a bin's mean IoU is
the area-weighted mean over its glaciers and its percentiles are area-weighted too.
Weighting by scope pixels instead (glacier pixels plus the non-glacier pixels within
250 m) would give the smallest glaciers far more weight than their ice: their 250 m
surroundings are many times their own area, and their IoU is low, as a one-pixel
outline error is a large share of a few hundred pixels.
Glaciers straddling two cross-validation folds are left out, since two models predict
them. The bins are chosen so that each holds a similar number of glacier pixels;
glaciers without any debris are too few to stand alone and share the lowest bin. Only
three inputs are drawn, GLACE with coherence only, backscatter only and both, as the
figure is about how much each measurement loses on debris-covered ice; the other
inputs are in the table.

```{python}
DEBRIS_FIGURE = f"{TABLE_NAME}-debris-cover"  # saved as {DEBRIS_FIGURE}.pdf in FIGURE_DIR
# Feature set -> (label, colour), left to right in each bin. All are GLACE, which the
# caption says, so the labels are the table's GLACE row labels, except for all_ctx: the
# table's "All layers" is read against its Layers column, which the figure lacks, so the
# figure names what the two others are subsets of. Coherence and backscatter take the
# colours of separability-overview.qmd, their combination a dark grey.
DEBRIS_SETS = {
    "all_ctx": ("Coherence + backscatter", "0.25"),
    "coh_dual_ctx": (SETS["coh_dual_ctx"], "#a49"),
    "rtc_dual_ctx": (SETS["rtc_dual_ctx"], "#4a9"),
}
DEBRIS_EDGES = [0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, np.inf]  # right-open, so the last takes 100 %
DEBRIS_LABELS = ["0–5", "5–10", "10–20", "> 20"]  # the unit is in the axis label
QUANTILES = {"q10": 0.10, "q25": 0.25, "q50": 0.50, "q75": 0.75, "q90": 0.90}
DODGE = 0.45  # width across which a bin's boxes are spread, in bins
BOX_ALPHA = 0.35  # of the box fill; the outline stays opaque
GRID_WIDTH = 0.4  # of the horizontal gridlines, as in separability-overview.qmd
LABEL_BIN = 0  # the bin whose columns carry the set labels, below their lowest whisker
LABEL_PAD = 0.02  # between a whisker's end and its label, in IoU

MM = 1 / 25.4
FIG_WIDTH = 120.0  # mm, 1.5 columns
FIG_HEIGHT = 70.0  # mm


def weighted_quantile(values: np.ndarray, weights: np.ndarray, q: float) -> float:
    """Quantile of ``values`` with each value counted by its weight (midpoint rule)."""
    order = np.argsort(values)
    v, w = values[order], weights[order]
    cdf = (np.cumsum(w) - 0.5 * w) / w.sum()
    return float(np.interp(q, cdf, v))


def bin_stats(d: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Glacier-pixel-weighted mean and percentiles of the IoU of one bin's glaciers."""
    iou, n = d["iou"].to_numpy(), d["glacier_pixels"].to_numpy()
    stats = {"iou": np.average(iou, weights=n)}
    stats |= {k: weighted_quantile(iou, n, q) for k, q in QUANTILES.items()}
    return pd.Series(stats)


glaciers = store.read_parquet(store.glaciers_path(RUN))
glaciers = glaciers[
    (glaciers.model == MODEL) & glaciers.feature_set.isin(DEBRIS_SETS) & ~glaciers.straddles_fold
]
per_glacier = glaciers.pivot_table(
    index=["feature_set", "gid", "debris_fraction", "n"], columns="metric", values="value"
).reset_index()
per_glacier["glacier_pixels"] = per_glacier["n"] * per_glacier["prevalence"]
per_glacier["bin"] = pd.cut(
    per_glacier["debris_fraction"], DEBRIS_EDGES, labels=DEBRIS_LABELS, right=False
)
debris = (
    per_glacier.groupby(["feature_set", "bin"], observed=False)
    .apply(bin_stats, include_groups=False)
    .reset_index()
)
```

### Bin sizes

Glaciers, scope pixels and glacier pixels per bin (the same for every feature set),
in thousands of pixels.

```{python}
first = per_glacier[per_glacier["feature_set"] == next(iter(DEBRIS_SETS))]
sizes = first.groupby("bin", observed=False).agg(
    glaciers=("gid", "size"),
    scope_pixels_k=("n", "sum"),
    glacier_pixels_k=("glacier_pixels", "sum"),
)
sizes[["scope_pixels_k", "glacier_pixels_k"]] = (
    sizes[["scope_pixels_k", "glacier_pixels_k"]] / 1e3
).round()
sizes["glacier_pixel_share"] = (sizes["glacier_pixels_k"] / sizes["glacier_pixels_k"].sum()).round(
    3
)
sizes.astype({"scope_pixels_k": int, "glacier_pixels_k": int})
```

### Figure

Boxes span the 25th to the 75th percentile, the line is the median, the dot the mean
and the whiskers reach from the 10th to the 90th percentile. The whiskers are not
Tukey's 1.5 × IQR, whose outliers would be single glaciers and so ignore the
weighting; no outliers are drawn. Each input is labelled below its lowest whisker in
the first bin instead of in a legend.

```{python}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(FIG_WIDTH * MM, FIG_HEIGHT * MM), layout="constrained")
k = len(DEBRIS_SETS)
offsets = (np.arange(k) - (k - 1) / 2) * DODGE / k
bins = np.arange(len(DEBRIS_LABELS))
for offset, (fs, (label, color)) in zip(offsets, DEBRIS_SETS.items()):
    part = debris[debris["feature_set"] == fs].set_index("bin").reindex(DEBRIS_LABELS)
    stats = [
        {"med": r.q50, "q1": r.q25, "q3": r.q75, "whislo": r.q10, "whishi": r.q90, "mean": r.iou}
        for r in part.itertuples()
    ]
    ax.bxp(
        stats,
        positions=bins + offset,
        widths=0.8 * DODGE / k,
        showfliers=False,
        showmeans=True,
        patch_artist=True,
        manage_ticks=False,
        boxprops={"facecolor": to_rgba(color, BOX_ALPHA), "edgecolor": color, "linewidth": 0.8},
        medianprops={"color": color, "linewidth": 1.2},
        whiskerprops={"color": color, "linewidth": 0.8},
        capprops={"color": color, "linewidth": 0.8},
        meanprops={
            "marker": "o",
            "markersize": 2.5,
            "markerfacecolor": color,
            "markeredgecolor": "white",
            "markeredgewidth": 0.4,
        },
    )
    # The input's label hangs vertically below its lower whisker in the label bin
    ax.text(
        LABEL_BIN + offset,
        part["q10"].iloc[LABEL_BIN] - LABEL_PAD,
        label,
        rotation=90,
        ha="center",
        va="top",
        color=color,
        fontweight="bold",
    )
ax.set_xticks(bins, DEBRIS_LABELS)
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(DEBRIS_LABELS) - 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
add_grid(ax, axis="y", linewidth=GRID_WIDTH)
ax.set_xlabel("Debris cover (% of glacier area)")
ax.set_ylabel("IoU per glacier")
with (FIGURE_DIR / f"{DEBRIS_FIGURE}.pdf").open("wb") as f:
    fig.savefig(f, format="pdf")
```

```{python}
debris.pivot(index="feature_set", columns="bin", values="iou").reindex(list(DEBRIS_SETS)).round(3)
```
